1: The prouerbes of Solomon the sonne of Dauid, kyng of Israel
To learne wisdome and instruction, & to perceaue the wordes of vnderstandyng
To receaue the instruction of wisdome, iustice, iudgement, and equitie
To geue wyt vnto the simple, and that the young men myght haue knowledge and vnderstandyng
The wise man wyll geue eare, and wyll come by more wisdome, and he that is endued with vnderstanding shal attayne vnto [wise] counsayles
To vnderstande a parable, and the interpretation therof, the wordes of the wise, and their darke speaches
The feare of the Lorde is the begynnyng of knowledge: but fooles dispise wisdome and instruction
My sonne, heare thy fathers doctrine, & forsake not the lawe of thy mother
For they shalbe an encrease of grace vnto thy head, and [as] a chayne about thy necke
My sonne, if sinners entice thee, consent not vnto them
If they say, come with vs, let vs lay wayte for blood, and lurke priuily for the innocent without a cause
Let vs swallowe them vp lyke the graue quicke and whole, as those that go downe into the pit
So shall we finde all maner of costly riches, and fill our houses with spoyles
Cast in thy lot among vs, and let vs all haue one purse
My sonne, walke not thou with them, refrayne thy foote from their wayes
For their feete runne to euyll, and are hasty to shed blood
But [as] in vayne, the nette is layde foorth before the birdes eyes
So these lay wayte for the blood of them, and lye priuily for their liues
Such [are] the wayes of euery one that is greedie of gayne, who taketh away the life of the owner therof
Wisdome cryeth without, and putteth foorth her voyce in the streetes
She calleth before the congregation in the open gates, and sheweth her wordes through the citie, saying
O ye children, howe long wyll ye loue childishnesse? howe long wyll the scorners delite in scornyng, and the vnwise hate knowledge
O turne you at my correction: lo I wyll expresse my mynde vnto you, and make you vnderstande my wordes
Because I haue called, and ye refused, I haue stretched out my hande, and no man regarded
But all my counsels haue ye dispised, and set my correction at naught
Therfore wyll I also laugh at your destruction, and mocke you, when the thyng that ye feare commeth vpon you
Euen when the thyng that ye be afraide of falleth in sodenly like a storme, and your miserie lyke a tempest, yea when trouble and heauinesse commeth vpon you
Then shall they call vpon me, but I wyll not aunswere: they shall seeke me early, but they shall not finde me
And that because they hated knowledge, and did not choose the feare of the Lorde
They woulde none of my counsayle, but dispised all my correction
Therfore shall they eate of the fruite of their owne way, and be fylled with their owne inuentions
For the turnyng away of the vnwise shall slay them, and the prosperitie of fooles shall destroy them
But whoso hearkeneth vnto me, shal dwell safely, and be sure from any feare of euyll
2: My sonne, if thou wylt receaue my wordes, and lay vp my commaundementes within thee
That thou wylt encline thine eares vnto wisdome: applye thine heart then to vnderstandyng
For if thou cryest after wisdome, and cryest for knowledge
If thou seekest for her as for siluer, and searchest for her as for treasures
Then shalt thou vnderstand the feare of the Lorde, and finde the knowledge of God
For the Lorde geueth wisdome, out of his mouth commeth knowledge and vnderstandyng
He stirreth vp health for the righteous: and defendeth them that walke vprightly
That they may kepe the right path: and he preserueth the way of such as do serue him with godlinesse
Then shalt thou vnderstande righteousnesse, and iudgement, and equitie, yea and euery good path
When wisdome entreth into thine heart, and thy soule deliteth in knowledge
Then shall counsayle preserue thee, and vnderstandyng shall kepe thee
That thou mayest be deliuered from the euyll way, and from the man that speaketh frowarde thynges
From such as leaue the wayes of righteousnesse, to walke in the wayes of darknesse
Which reioyce in doyng naught, and delite in the wickednesse of the euyll
Whose wayes are croked, and they frowarde in their pathes
That thou mayest be deliuered also from the straunge woman, and from her that is not thine owne, which geueth sweete wordes
Forsaketh the husbande of her youth, & forgetteth the couenaunt of her God
For her house is enclined vnto death, and her pathes vnto hell
All they that go in vnto her, come not agayne, neither take they holde of the way of lyfe
Therfore walke thou in the way of such as be vertuous, & kepe the pathes of the righteous
For the iust shal dwell in the lande, and they that be perfect shall remayne in it
But the vngodly shall be cut of from the earth: and the wicked doers shalbe rooted out of it
3: My sonne, forget not thou my lawe, but see that thine heart kepe my commaundementes
For they shal prolong the dayes and yeres of thy lyfe, and bryng thee peace
Let mercie and faithfulnesse neuer go from thee: binde them about thy necke, and write them in the tables of thyne heart
So shalt thou finde fauour and good vnderstandyng in the sight of God and men
Put thy trust in God with all thine heart: & leane not vnto thine owne wit
In all thy wayes acknowledge him, and he shall order thy goynges
Be not wise in thine owne conceipt: but feare the Lorde, and depart from euyll
So shall thy nauell be whole, and thy bones strong
Honour the Lorde with thy substaunce, and with the firstlynges of all thyne encrease
So shall thy barnes be filled with plenteousnesse, and thy presses shall flowe ouer with sweete wine
My sonne refuse not the chastening of the Lorde, neither faynt when thou art corrected of hym
For whom the Lorde loueth, him he chasteneth, and yet deliteth in him, euen as a father in his owne sonne
Well is hym that findeth wysdome, and getteth vnderstandyng
For the marchaundise of it, is better then the marchaundise of siluer, and the gayne therof [is better] then golde
She is more worth then pretious stones: and all the thinges that thou canst desire, are not to be compared vnto her
In her right hande is long life, and in her left hande riches and honour
Her wayes are pleasaunt wayes, and all her pathes are peaceable
She is a tree of lyfe to them that lay holde vpon her: and blessed is he that kepeth her fast
With wysdome hath the Lorde layde the foundation of the earth, and thorow vnderstanding hath he stablished the heauens
Thorow his knowledge the deapthes are broken vp, and the cloudes droppe downe the deawe
My sonne, let not these thinges depart from thyne eyes, but kepe wysdome and vnderstanding
So they shall be lyfe vnto thy soule, and grace vnto thy mouth
Then shalt thou walke safely in thy way, and thy foote shall not stumble
If thou sleepest, thou shalt not be afraide: but shalt take thy rest, and sleepe sweetely
Thou shalt not be afraide of any sodayne feare, neither for the violent rushing in of the vngodly when it commeth
For the Lorde shall stande by thy side, & kepe thy foote that thou be not taken
Withdraw no good thyng from them that haue nede, so long as thyne hande is able to do it
Say not vnto thy neyghbour, go thy way and come agayne, and to morowe wyll I geue thee: where as thou hast nowe to geue hym
Intende no hurt against thy neyghbour, seing he hopeth to dwell in rest by thee
Striue not with any man without a cause, where as he hath done thee no harme
Folowe not a wicked man, and chose none of his wayes
For the Lord abhorreth the froward: but his counsayle is among the righteous
The curse of the Lord is in the house of the vngodly: but he blesseth the dwellinges of the righteous
As for the scornfull, doth he not laugh them to scorne? but he geueth grace vnto the lowly
The wyse shall haue honour in possession: but shame is the promotion that fooles shall haue
4: Heare O ye chyldren a fatherly instruction, & take good heede, that ye may learne vnderstanding
For I haue geuen you a good doctrine, forsake not ye my lawe
For when I my selfe was my fathers deare sonne, and tenderly beloued of my mother
He taught me also and sayde vnto me, let thyne heart receaue my wordes, kepe my commaundementes and thou shalt liue
Get thee wysdome, and get thee vnderstanding: forget not the wordes of my mouth, and shrinke not from them
Forsake her not, and she shall preserue thee, loue her, and she shall kepe thee
The chiefe poynt of wysdome, is to possesse wysdome: and before all thy goodes to get thee vnderstanding
Make much of her, and she shall promote thee, yea if thou embrace her, she shall bryng thee vnto honour
She shal beautifie thy head with manyfolde graces, and garnishe thee with a crowne of glory
Heare my sonne, and receaue my wordes, and the yeres of thy life shalbe many
I haue shewed thee the way of wysdome, & led thee into the right pathes
So that if thou goest in them, there shall no straitnesse hinder thee: & when thou runnest, thou shalt not fall
Take fast holde of doctrine, and let her not go: kepe her, for she is thy life
Come not in the pathe of the vngodlye, and walke not in the way of the wicked
Abhorre it and go not therein, depart aside, and passe ouer by it
For they sleepe not except they haue done mischiefe: and sleepe is taken from them, vntyll they haue done harme
For they eate the bread of wickednes, and drinke the wine of robberie
The path of the righteous shineth, as the light that is euer bryghter and bryghter vnto the perfect day
But the way of the vngodly is as the darkenesse, they knowe not where they fall
My sonne marke my wordes, and encline thyne eare vnto my sayinges
Let them not depart from thine eyes, but kepe them euen in the middest of thyne heart
For they are life vnto those that finde them, and health vnto all their bodyes
Kepe thyne heart with all diligence, for out of it issueth lyfe
Put away from thee a frowarde mouth, and let the lippes of slaunder be farre from thee
Let thyne eyes beholde that thyng that is right, and let thyne eye liddes loke straight before thee
Ponder the path of thy feete, and let all thy wayes be ordred aright
Turne not aside, neither to the right hande nor to the left: but wihholde thy foote from euyll
5: My sonne geue heede vnto my wisdome, and bowe thyne eare vnto my prudence
That thou mayest regarde good counsell, and that thy lippes may kepe knowledge
For the lippes of a straunge woman are a dropping hony combe, and her throte is more glistering then oyle
But at the laste she is as bitter as wormewood, and as sharpe as a two edged sworde
Her feete go downe vnto death, and her steppes pearce thorowe vnto hell
Perchaunce thou wylt ponder the path of her lyfe: so vnstedfast are her wayes that thou canst not know them
Heare me nowe therefore O ye chyldren, and depart not from the wordes of my mouth
Kepe thy way farre from her, & come not nigh the doores of her house
That thou geue not thy honour vnto other, and thy yeres to the cruell
That other men be not filled with thy vertues, and that thy labours come not in a straunge house
Yea, that thou mourne not at the last, when thou hast spent thy bodye and lustie youth, and then say
Alas, why hated I nurture? why did my heart dispise correction
Wherefore was not I obedient vnto the voyce of my teachers, and hearkened not vnto them that enfourmed me
I was come almost into all misfortune, in the middest of the multitude and congregation
Drinke of the water of thyne owne well, and of the riuers that runne out of thyne owne spring
Let thy welles flowe out abrode, that there may be riuers of waters in the streates
But let them be onlye thyne owne, and not straungers with thee
Let thy well be blessed, and be glad with the wyfe of thy youth
Let her be as the louyng Hinde and pleasaunt Roe: let her breastes alway satisfie thee, and holde thee euer content with her loue
Why wylt thou my sonne haue pleasure in a straunge woman, and embrace the bosome of a straunger
For euery mans wayes are open in the sight of the Lord, and he pondereth all their goynges
The wickednes of the vngodly shall catche him selfe, and with the snares of his owne sinne shall he be trapped
He shall dye without amendement, and for his great foolishnes he shall go astray
6: My sonne if thou be suretie for thy neyghbour, and hast fastened thyne hande for another man
Thou art bounde with thine owne wordes, and taken with thine owne speach
Therfore my sonne do this, and thou shalt be discharged: When thou art come into thy neyghbours daunger, go thy wayes then soone, humble thy selfe, and with thy frendes intreate [thy creditour.
Let not thyne eyes sleepe, nor thyne eye liddes slumber
Saue thy self as a Doe from the hand of the [hunter] and as a byrde from the hande of the fouler
Go to the emmet thou sluggarde, consider her wayes, and learne to be wyse
She hath no guyde, nor ouerseer, nor ruler
Yet in the sommer she prouideth her meate, and gathereth her foode together in the haruest
Howe long wylt thou sleepe thou sluggishe man? When wylt thou aryse out of thy sleepe
Yea, sleepe on still a litle, slumber a litle, folde thyne handes together yet a litle that thou mayest sleepe
So shall pouertie come vnto thee as one that trauayleth by the way, and necessitie like a weaponed man
An vngodly person, a wicked man, goeth with a frowarde mouth
He winketh with his eyes, he tokeneth with his feete, he teacheth with his fingers
He is euer imagining mischiefe and frowardnes in his heart, and causeth discorde
Therefore shall his destruction come hastyly vpon hym, sodainly shall he be all to broken, and not be healed
These sixe thinges doth the Lorde hate, and the seuenth he vtterly abhorreth
A proude loke, a lying tongue, handes that shed innocent blood
An heart that goeth about wicked imaginations, feete that be swyft in running to mischiefe
A false witnesse that bringeth vp lyes, and hym that soweth discorde among brethren
My sonne, kepe thy fathers commaundement, and forsake not the lawe of thy mother
Tye them continually in thyne heart, and bynde them about thy necke
That shall leade thee when thou goest, preserue thee when thou art asleepe, and when thou awakest talke with thee
For the commaundement is a lanterne, and the lawe a light: yea chastening and nurture is the way of life
That they may kepe thee from the euyll woman, and from the flattering tongue of the straunge woman
Lust not after her beautie in thyne heart, lest thou be taken with her fayre lokes
By an harlot [a man is brought] to beg his bread, and a woman wyll hunte for the pretious life of man
May a man take fire in his bosome, and his clothes not be brent
Or can one go vpon hotte coales, and his feete not be brent
Euen so, whosoeuer goeth in to his neyghbours wife and toucheth her, can not be vngiltie
Men do not vtterly despise a thiefe that stealeth to satisfie his soule, when he is hungrie
But if he may be gotten, he restoreth agayne seuen tymes as muche, or els he maketh recompence with all the good of his house
But whoso committeth adultrie with a woman, lacketh vnderstanding: and he that doth it, destroyeth his owne soule
He getteth him selfe a plague and dishonour, and his reproche shall neuer be put out
For the ielousie and wrath of the man wyll not be entreated
No though thou wouldest offer hym great gyftes to make amendes, he wyll not receaue them
7: My sonne kepe my words, and lay vp my commaundements by thee
Kepe my commaundementes & my lawe, euen as the apple of thyne eye, and thou shalt liue
Binde them vpon thy fingers, and wryte them in the table of thyne heart
Say vnto wysdome, thou art my sister: and call vnderstanding thy kinsewoman
That they may kepe thee from the straunge woman, and from the forraine woman which geueth sweete wordes
For at the windowe of my house I loked through the windowe
And behelde among the simple people and among the chyldren a young man voyde of wyt
Goyng ouer the streate by the corner in the way towarde her hous
In the twylight of the euening, when it began nowe to be night and darke
And behold there met hym a woman with open tokens of an harlot, onlye her heart was hid
She was full of loude wordes and redye to dallie, whose feete coulde not abide in the house
Nowe is she without, nowe in the streates, and lyeth in wayte at euery corner
She caught hym and kissed him, and was not ashamed, saying
I had a vowe of peace offeringes to pay, and this day I perfourme it
Therefore came I foorth to meete thee, that I might seeke thy face, and so haue I founde thee
I haue deckt my bed with coueringes of tapessarie, and clothes of Egypt
My bed haue I made to smell of Myrre, Aloes, and Cinamon
Come let vs take our fill of loue vntyll the morning, and let vs solace our selues with the pleasures of loue
For the good man is not at home, he is gone farre of
He hath taken the bagge of money with hym, and wyll returne at the appointed solempne feast
Thus with many sweete wordes she ouercame him, and with her flattering lippes she entised hym
Sodainly he folowed her, as it were an oxe led to the slaughter, and lyke as it were a foole [that laugheth] when he goeth to the stockes to be punished
So long tyll she had wounded his lyuer with her dart: lyke as if a byrde hasted to the snare, not knowing that the perill of his life lieth thervpon
Heare me now therfore O my chylde, and marke the wordes of my mouth
Let not thyne heart wander in her wayes, and be not thou deceaued in her pathes
For many one hath she wounded and cast downe, yea many a strong man hath ben slaine by the meanes of her
Her house is the way vnto hell, and bryng men downe into the chaumbers of death
8: Doth not wysdome crye? doth not vnderstanding put foorth her voyce
She standeth in the top of high places, by the way in the place of the pathes
She cryeth at the gates of the citie, at the entrye of the doores
It is you O ye men [saith she] whom I call, vnto the chyldren of men do I lyft vp my voyce
Take heede vnto knowledge O ye ignoraunt, be ye wise in heart O ye fooles
Geue eare, for I wyll speake of great matters, and open my lippes to tell thinges that be right
For my mouth shall be talking of the trueth, and my lippes abhorre vngodlynesse
All the wordes of my mouth are righteous, there is no frowardnes nor falsehood in them
They are all playne to suche as wyll vnderstande, and right to them that finde knowledge
Receaue my doctrine and not siluer, and knowledge rather then fine golde
For wysdome is more worth then pretious stones, yea all thinges that thou canst desire, may not be compared vnto it
I wysdome dwell with counsell, and finde out knowledge and vnderstanding
The feare of the Lorde abhorreth wickednes, pryde, disdayne, and the euil way, and a mouth that speaketh wicked thinges I vtterly abhorre
Counsell is mine, and direction, I am vnderstanding, and I haue strength
Through me kinges raigne, and princes make iust lawes
By me princes beare rule, and noble men do iudge the earth
I am louing vnto those that loue me: and they that seeke me early, shall finde me
Riches and honour are with me, yea durable riches and righteousnes
My fruite is better then golde and pretious stones, and mine encrease more worth then fine siluer
I wyll guyde thee in the way of righteousnes, and in the midst of the pathes of iudgement
That I maye stablishe the inhetaunce of them that loue me, and encrease their treasure
The Lorde him selfe had me in possession in the beginning of his wayes, or euer he began his workes aforetime
I haue ben ordayned from euerlasting, and from the beginning or euer the earth was made
When I was borne there were neither depthes nor springes of water
Before the foundations of the mountaines were layde: yea before all hilles, was I borne
The earth, and all that is vpon the earth was not yet made, no not the dust it selfe
For when he made the heauens, I was present, when he compassed the deapthes about
When he hanged the cloudes aboue, when he fastened the springes of the deepe
When he shut the sea within certaine boundes, that the waters should not go ouer their markes that he commaunded: when he layde the foundations of the earth
I was with him ordring all thinges, deliting dayly and reioysyng alway before hym
As for the rounde compasse of this worlde I make it ioyfull: for my delite is to be among the chyldren of men
Therefore hearken vnto me: O ye chyldren, blessed are they that kepe my wayes
O geue eare vnto nurture, be wyse, and refuse it not
Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching dayly at my gates, and geuing attendaunce at the postes of my doores
For whoso findeth me, findeth life, and shall obtaine fauour of the Lorde
But whoso offendeth against me, hurteth his owne soule: and they that hate me, are the louers of death
9: Wysdome hath buylded her house, and hewen out seuen pillers
She hath kylled her victuals, powred out her wine, and prepared her table
She hath sent foorth her maydens to crye vpon the highest place of the citie
Who so is without knowledge, let him come hither: And to the vnwise she said
O come on your way, eate my bread, and drinke my wine [whiche] I haue powred out for you
Forsake foolishnes, and ye shall lyue: and see that ye go in the way of vnderstandyng
Whoso reproueth a scornefull person, getteth him selfe dishonour: and he that rebuketh the vngodly, stayneth hym selfe
Reproue not a scorner, lest he owe thee euyll will: but rebuke a wyse man, and he wyll loue thee
Geue a discrete man but an occasion, and he wyll be the wyser: teache a righteous man, and he wyll encrease in knowledge
The feare of the Lorde is the beginning of wisdome: and the knowledge of holy thinges, is vnderstanding
For thorowe me thy dayes shalbe prolonged, and the yeres of thy life shall be many
If thou be wise, thy wysdome shal do thy selfe good: but if thou thinkest scorne therof, it shalbe thine owne harme
A foolishe retchlesse woman full of wordes, and suche a one as hath no knowledge
Sitteth at the doore of her house, and in the hye places of the citie
To call such as go by, and that walke straight in their wayes
Who so is ignoraunt [sayeth she] let hym come hyther: and to the vnwyse she saith
Stolen waters are sweete, & the bread that is priuily eaten, hath a good taste
And he doth not consider that they are but dead whiche be there, and that her ghestes are in the deepe of hell
10: A wyse sonne maketh a glad father: but an vndiscrete sonne is an heauinesse vnto his mother
Treasures that are wickedly gotten, profite nothing: but righteousnesse deliuereth from death
The Lorde wyll not let the soule of the righteous suffer hunger: but he taketh away the richesse of the vngodly
An idle hande maketh poore: but a quicke labouring hande maketh riche
Who so gathereth in sommer is wyse: but he that is sluggishe in haruest, bringeth hym selfe to confusion
Blessinges are vpon the head of the righteous: and the mouth of the vngodly kepeth mischiefe in secrete
The memoriall of the iust shall haue a good report: but the name of the vngodly shall stincke
A wyse man wyll receaue warning: but a prating foole shalbe punished
He that walketh vprightly, walketh surely: but whoso goeth a wrong way, shalbe knowen
He that winketh with his eye, wyll cause sorowe: but he that hath a foolishe mouth, shalbe beaten
The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but the mouth of the vngodly kepeth mischiefe in secrete
Hatred stirreth vp strifes: but loue couereth the multitude of sinnes
In the lippes of him that hath vnderstanding, a man shall finde wysdome: but the rod belongeth to the backe of the foolishe
Wyse men lay vp knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish is nye destruction
The riche mans goodes are his strong holde: but their owne pouertie feareth the poore
The labour of the righteous [tendeth] to lyfe: but the fruites of the vngodly, to sinne
Nurture kepeth the way of lyfe: but he that refuseth to be nurtured, deceaueth hym selfe
He that hydeth hatred with lying lippes, and he that speaketh slaunder, is a foole
Where much babblyng is, there must needes be offence: and he that refrayneth his lippes, is wyse
The tongue of the iust man is as tried siluer: but the heart of the vngodly is a thyng of naught
The lippes of the ryghteous feede a whole multitude: but fooles shall dye in their owne follie
The blessyng of the Lorde maketh riche: and bryngeth no sorowe of heart with it
A foole doth wickedly, and maketh but a sport of it: but wisdome ruleth the man that hath vnderstandyng
The thing that the vngodly is afraide of, shall come vpon hym: but the ryghteous shall haue their desire
As the tempest, so passeth away the vngodly and is not: but the ryghteous remayneth sure for euer
As vineger is to the teeth, & as smoke is vnto the eyes: euen so is a sluggishe person to them that sendeth him foorth
The feare of the Lorde maketh a long lyfe: but the yeres of the vngodly shalbe shortened
The patient abydyng of the righteous shalbe turned to gladnesse: but the hope of the vngodly shall perishe
The way of the Lord geueth courage vnto the godly: but it is a feare for wicked doers
The ryghteous shall neuer be ouerthrowen: but the vngodly shall not remayne in the lande
The mouth of the iust wyll be talking of wisdome: but the tongue of the frowarde shall be cut out
The lippes of the ryghteous vtter that which is acceptable: but the mouth of the vngodly [speaketh] frowarde thynges
11: A false ballaunce is an abomination vnto the Lorde: but a true wayght pleaseth him
Where pryde is, there is shame also and confusion: but wheras is lowlinesse, there is wisdome
The innocent dealyng of the iust shall leade them: but the wickednesse of the offendours shalbe their owne destruction
Riches helpe not in the day of vengeaunce: but ryghteousnesse deliuereth from death
The ryghteousnesse of the innocent ordereth his way: but the vngodly shall fall in his owne wickednesse
The righteousnesse of the iust shall delyuer them: but the wicked shalbe taken in their owne vngodlynesse
When an vngodly man dyeth, his hope is gone: the confidence of riches shall perishe
The ryghteous shalbe delyuered out of trouble: and the vngodly shall come in his steade
The dissembler with his mouth hurteth his neighbour: but through knowledge shall the iust be deliuered
When it goeth well with the ryghteous the citie is mery: and when the vngodly perishe there is gladnesse
In the blessyng of the ryghteous the citie is exalted: but it is ouerthrowen by the mouth of the wicked
A foole slaundereth his neyghbour: but a wise man holdeth his peace
A dissemblyng person wyll discouer priuie thynges: but he that is of a faythfull heart wyll kepe counsayle
Where no counsayle is, there the people decay: but wheras many are that can geue counsayle, there is wealth
He that is suretie for a straunger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretishyp is sure
A gratious woman getteth honour: but the strong men attayne riches
He that is mercifull, doth hym selfe a benefite: but who so hurteth his neyghbour, is a tiraunt
The vngodly worketh deceiptfull workes: but he that soweth righteousnesse shall receaue a sure rewarde
Lyke as ryghteousnesse bringeth lyfe: euen so to cleaue vnto euyll, bryngeth death
The Lorde abhorreth them that be of a corrupt heart: but he hath pleasure in them that are of an vndefiled conuersation
Though hand be ioyned in hande, yet the wicked shall not escape: but the seede of the ryghteous shalbe preserued
A faire woman without discrete maners, is lyke a ryng of golde in a swines snoute
The desire of the ryghteous is acceptable: but the hope of the vngodly is indignation
Some man geueth out his goodes and is the richer: but the niggarde hauyng inough, wyll depart from nothyng, and yet is euer in pouertie
He that is liberall in geuyng, shall haue plentie: and he that watereth, shalbe watered also hym selfe
Who so hoordeth vp his corne, shalbe cursed among the people: but blessyng shall lyght vpon his head that geueth foode
He that searcheth for good thynges fyndeth fauour: but who so seketh after mischiefe, it shall happen vnto hym
He that trusteth in his riches shall haue a fall: but the ryghteous shall florishe as the greene leafe
Who so maketh disquietnesse in his owne house, he shal haue winde for his heritage: and the foole shalbe seruaunt to the wise
The fruite of the ryghteous is a tree of life: and he that winneth mens soules is wise
If the ryghteous be recompensed vpon earth: howe much more then the vngodly and the sinner
12: Who so loueth correction loueth knowledge: but he that hateth to be reproued is a foole
A good man is acceptable vnto the Lorde: but the wicked imaginer wyll he condempne
A man can not endure in vngodlinesse: but the roote of the ryghteous shall not be moued
A huswifely woman is a crowne vnto her husbande: but she that behaueth her selfe vnhonestly, is as corruption in his bones
The thoughtes of the ryghteous are ryght: but the imaginations of the vngodly are deceptfull
The talkyng of the vngodly is howe they may lay wayte for blood: but the mouth of the righteous will deliuer the
God ouerturneth the [estate of the] wicked, and they stande not: but the house of the ryghteous shall stande
A man shalbe commended for his wisdome: but a foole shalbe dispised
He that is dispised and is yet his owne man, is better then the glorious that lacketh bread
A ryghteous man regardeth the lyfe of his cattell: but the vngodly haue cruell heartes
He that tylleth his lande, shall haue plenteousnesse of bread: but he that foloweth idlenesse is a very foole
The desire of the vngodly is a net of euyls: but the roote of the ryghteous bryngeth foorth fruite
The wicked falleth into the snare thorowe the malice of his owne mouth: but the iust shall escape out of all perill
Man shalbe satisfied with good thinges: by the fruite of his mouth, and after the workes of his handes shall he be rewarded
The way of a foole is strayght in his owne eyes: but he that hearkeneth vnto counsayle is wise
A foole vttereth his wrath in all the haste: but a discrete man couereth his owne shame
A iust man wyll tell the trueth and shewe the thyng that is ryght: but a false witnesse deceaueth
A slaunderous person pricketh lyke a sworde: but a wise mans tongue is wholsome
The lippe of trueth shalbe stable for euer: but a dissemblyng tongue is soone chaunged
Deceipt is in the heart of them that imagine euyll: but to the counsaylers of peace shalbe ioy
There shall no aduersitie happen vnto the iust: but the vngodly shalbe fylled with miserie
The Lorde abhorreth lying lippes: but they that deale truely please hym
A discrete man doth hyde knowledge: but the heart of fooles blabbeth out foolishnesse
A diligent hande shall beare rule: but the idle shalbe vnder tribute
Heauinesse discourageth the heart of man: but a good worde maketh it glad agayne
The ryghteous excelleth his neyghbour: but the way of the vngodly wyll deceaue them selues
The deciptfull man shall not coste that he toke in huntyng: but the riches of the iust man is of great value
In the way of ryghteousnesse there is life: & in the same way there is no death
13: A wise sonne [wil hearken] to his fathers warnyng: but he that is scorneful wil not heare when he is reproued
Of the fruite of a wise mans mouth shall eche man eate good thynges: but the wicked shall eate of the fruite of the transgressours
He that kepeth his mouth, kepeth his lyfe: but who so rashlye openeth his lippes, destroyeth hym selfe
The sluggarde woulde fayne haue and can not get [his desire:] but the soule of the diligent shall haue plentie
A ryghteous man abhorreth lyes: but the vngodly shameth hym selfe, and is put to scilence
Ryghteousnesse kepeth the innocent in the way: but vngodlinesse doth ouerthrowe the sinner
Some men make them selues riche though they haue nothyng: agayne, some make them selues poore hauyng great riches
With goodes a man redeemeth his life: and the poore wyll not be reproued
The lyght of the ryghteous maketh ioyfull: but the candell of the vngodly shalbe put out
Among the proude there is euer strife: but with the well aduised is wisdome
Uaynly gotten goodes are soone spent: but they that be gathered together with the hande, shall encrease
Hope deferred greeueth the heart: but whe the desire cometh, it is a tree of life
Who so dispiseth the worde, shall perishe for the same: but he that feareth the commaundement, shall haue the rewarde
The lawe of the wise is a well of life, to auoyde from the snares of death
Good vnderstandyng geueth fauour: but harde is the way of the dispisers
A wise man doth all thynges with discretion: but a foole wyll declare his follie
An vngodly messenger falleth into mischiefe: but a faythfull embassadour is as health
He that thinketh scorne to be refourmed, commeth to pouertie and shame: but who so regardeth correction, shall come to honour
When a desire is brought to passe, it deliteth the soule: but fooles count it abhomination to depart from euyll
He that goeth in the companie of wise men, shalbe wise: but who so is a companion of fooles, shalbe afflicted
Mischiefe foloweth vpon sinners: but the righteous shal haue a good reward
He that is vertuous leaueth an heritaunce vnto his childers children, & the riches of ye sinner is layde vp for the iust
There is plenteousnesse of foode in the fieldes of the poore: but the fielde not well ordered, is without fruite
He that spareth the rodde, hateth his sonne: but who so loueth hym, chasteneth hym betymes
The righteous eateth and is satisfied: but the belly of the vngodly hath neuer enough
14: Wyse women vpholde their house: but a foolishe wyfe plucketh it downe
He that walketh vpryghtlye, feareth the Lorde: but he that turneth hym selfe from his wayes, dispiseth hym
In the mouth of the foolishe is the rodde of pryde: but the lippes of the wyse wyll preserue them
Where no oxen are, there the cribbe is emptie: but much encrease commeth by the toyle of the oxe
A faithfull witnesse will not dissemble: but a false recorde wyll make a lye
A scornfull body seketh wisdome, and fyndeth it not: but knowledge is easie vnto hym that wyll vnderstande
Get thee from a foolishe man, when thou perceauest not in hym the lippes of knowledge
The wisdome of the circumspect man, is to vnderstande his way: but the foolishnesse of the vnwise, deceaueth
Fooles make but a sport of sinne: but there is a fauourable loue among the ryghteous
The heart knoweth his owne soules bitternesse: and the straunger shall not be partaker of his ioy
The house of the vngodly shalbe ouerthrowen: but the tabernacle of the righteous shall florishe
There is a way which seemeth right vnto a man: but the ende therof are the wayes of death
The heart is sorowfull euen in laughter, and the ende of myrth is heauinesse
A backe slydyng heart shalbe fylled with his owne wayes: but a good man shall depart from hym
An ignorant body beleueth euery worde: but who so hath vnderstanding, loketh well to his goynges
A wyse man feareth, and departeth from euyll: but the foole is angry, and counteth hym selfe sure
An vnpatient man dealeth foolishly: but he that is well aduised, is hated [of the foole.
The ignoraunt haue foolishnesse in possession: but the wyse are crowned with knowledge
The euyll shall bowe them selues before the good: and the vngodly shall wayte at the gates of the ryghteous
The poore is hated euen of his owne neyghbours: but the riche hath many frendes
Who so dispiseth his neighbour, sinneth: but blessed is he that hath pitie of the poore
Without doubt they erre that worke wickednesse: but they that muse vpon good thynges, vnto such shall happen mercie and trueth
In euery labour there is some profite: but vayne wordes bryng foorth onely penurie
Riches are as a crowne vnto the wise: but the ignoraunce of fooles is very foolishnesse
A faythfull witnesse deliuereth soules: but a deceiptfull witnesse bryngeth foorth lyes
In the feare of the Lord is an assured strength: and his children are vnder a sure defence
The feare of the Lorde is a well of lyfe, to auoyde the snares of death
In the multitude of people is the kynges honour: but the decay of the people is the confusion of the prince
He that is patient hath much vnderstanding: but he that is soone displeased, exalteth foolishnesse
A mery heart is the lyfe of the body: but enuie consumeth away the bones
He that doth a poore man wrong, blasphemeth his maker: but who so honoureth him, hath pitie on the poore
The vngodly is cast away for his iniquitie: but the ryghteous hath a good hope, euen in death
Wisdome resteth in the heart of hym that hath vnderstandyng, and it shalbe knowen among them that are vnlearned
Righteousnesse setteth vp the people: but the sacrifice of the heathen is sinnefull
A discrete seruaunt is a pleasure vnto the kyng: but his wrath is agaynst hym that doth dishonour hym
15: A soft aunswere appeaseth wrath: but rough wordes stirre vp anger
The tongue of such as be wise vseth knoweledge aryght: as for a foolishe mouth it babbleth out nothyng but foolishnesse
The eyes of the Lorde in euery place, beholdeth both the good and the bad
A wholsome tongue is a tree of lyfe: but the frowardnesse therof doth make sad the spirite
A foole dispiseth his fathers correction: but he that taketh heede when he is reproued, shall haue the more vnderstandyng
The house of the ryghteous is full of riches: but in the fruites of the vngodly there is trouble
The lippes of the wise do sowe knowledge: but the heart of the foolishe do not so
The Lorde abhorreth the sacrifice of the vngodly: but the prayer of the righteous is acceptable vnto hym
The way of the vngodly is an abhomination vnto the Lorde: but who so foloweth righteousnesse, him he loueth
Correction is greeuous vnto hym that forsaketh the way: and who so hateth correction shall dye
Hell and destruction are before the Lorde: howe much more then the heartes of the children of men
A scornefull body loueth not one that rebuketh hym: neither wyll he come vnto the wyse
A mery heart maketh a chearfull countenaunce: but by the sorowe of the heart the mynde is heauy
The heart of hym that hath vnderstandyng doth seke knowledge: but the mouth of fooles is fed with foolishnesse
All the dayes of the poore are miserable: but a quiet heart is a continuall feast
Better is a litle with the feare of the Lorde: then great treasure, and trouble therwith
Better is a dynner of hearbes with loue, then a fat oxe with euyll wyll
An angry man stirreth vp strife: but he that is patient stylleth discorde
The way of a slouthfull man is as an hedge of thornes: but the way of the ryghteous is playne
A wyse sonne maketh a glad father: but a foolishe man dispiseth his mother
Foolishnesse is ioy to him that is destitute of knowledge: but a man of vnderstandyng walketh vprightly
Thoughtes without counsayle shall come to naught: but wheras men are that can geue good counsayle, there is stedfastnesse
A ioyfull thing it is to a man whe his counsayle is folowed: and howe good is a worde spoken in season
The way of lyfe is on hygh to the wise, that a man shoulde beware of hell beneath
The Lorde wyll breake downe the house of the proude: but he shall make fast the borders of the wydowe
The Lorde abhorreth the imaginations of the wicked: but the wordes of the pure are pleasaunt
The greedy couetous man rooteth vp his owne house: but who so hateth rewardes shall lyue
The heart of the ryghteous studyeth his aunswere afore: but the wicked mans mouth spueth out mischiefe
The Lorde is farre from the vngodly: but he heareth the prayer of the ryghteous
The clearnes of the eye reioyseth the heart, & a good name feedeth the bones
The eare that hearkeneth to the refourmation of lyfe, shall dwell among the wyse
He that refuseth to be refourmed, dispiseth his owne soule: but he that submitteth him selfe to correction, is wyse
The feare of the Lorde is the ryght science of wisdome, and lowlynesse goeth before honour
16: A man may wel purpose a thyng in his heart: but the aunswere of the tongue commeth of the Lorde
A man thynketh all his wayes to be cleane: but it is the Lorde that iudgeth the myndes
Commit thy workes vnto the Lorde: and what thou deuisest it shall prosper
The Lorde hath made all thynges for his owne sake: yea, the vngodly for the day of wrath
The Lorde abhorreth all such as be of a proude heart: and though hande be ioyned in hande, yet they shall not be vnpunished
With mercie and faythfulnesse sinnes be forgeuen: and by the feare of the Lorde euyll is eschewed
When a mans wayes please the Lord, he maketh his very enemies to be his frendes
Better it is to haue a litle with ryghteousnesse, then great rentes wrongfully gotten
A man deuiseth a way in his heart: but it is the Lorde that ordereth his goynges
When the prophecie is in the lippes of the kyng, his mouth shall not go wrong in iudgement
A true wayght and ballaunce are the Lordes iudgement: all the wayghtes of the bagge are his worke
Wicked doers are an abhomination to the kyng, for a kynges seate shoulde be holden vp with ryghteousnesse
Ryghteous lippes are pleasaunt vnto kynges, and them that speaketh the trueth shall he loue
The kinges displeasure is a messenger of death: but a wise man wyll pacifie hym
The chearfull countenaunce of the kyng is life: and his louyng fauour is as a cloude of the latter rayne
To haue wisdome in possession, is better then to haue golde: and to get vnderstandyng, is rather to be chosen then to haue siluer
The path of the ryghteous is to eschewe euyll, and who so loketh well to his wayes, kepeth his owne soule
Pryde goeth before destruction, and an hygh mynde before the fall
Better it is to be of humble mynde with the lowly, the to deuide the spoyles with the proude
He that handleth a matter wisely obteyneth good: and blessed is he that putteth his trust in the Lorde
Who so is wyse in heart, shalbe called prudent: and the sweetnesse of his lippes encreaseth learnyng
Vnderstandyng is a well of lyfe vnto hym that hath it: as for the chastenyng of fooles it is but foolishnesse
A wyse heart ordereth his mouth wisely, and ministreth learnyng vnto his lippes
Fayre wordes are an hony combe, a refresshyng of the mynde, and health of the bones
There is a way that men thynke to be ryght: but the ende therof leadeth vnto death
A troublous soule disquieteth her selfe, for her owne mouth hath brought her therto
An vngodly person stirreth vp euyll, and in his lippes he is as an hotte burnyng fyre
A frowarde body causeth strife: and he that is a blabbe of his tongue maketh deuision among princes
A wicked man beguyleth his neyghbour, and leadeth hym into the way that is not good
He shutteth his eyes to deuise mischiefe: and moueth his lippes to bryng euyll to passe
Age is a crowne of worshyp, yf it be founde in the way of ryghteousnesse
A patient man is better the one strong: and he that can rule hym selfe, is more worth then he that wynneth a citie
The lottes are cast into the lappe: but the orderyng therof standeth all in the Lorde
17: Better is a drye morsell with quietnesse, then a house full of fat offeryng with strife
A discrete seruaunt shall haue rule ouer a lewde sonne, and shal haue heritage with the brethren
As siluer is tryed in the fire, and golde in the furnace: so doth the Lorde proue the heartes
A wicked body geueth heede to false lippes, and a lyer geueth eare to a deceiptfull tongue
Who so scorneth the poore, blasphemeth his maker: and he that is glad at [another mans] hurt, shall not be vnpunished
Childers children are a crowne of the aged, and the fathers are the honour of the children
Speache of aucthoritie becommeth not a foole, much lesse a lying mouth then beseemeth a prince
A gyft is as a precious stone vnto hym that hath it: but vnto whom soeuer it turneth, it maketh hym vnwise
Who so couereth a fault, procureth loue: but he that discloseth it, deuideth very frendes
One reproofe more feareth a wise man, then an hundred stripes doth a foole
A seditious person seketh mischiefe, and a cruell messenger shalbe sent agaynst hym
It were better to meete a shee beare robbed of her whelpes, then a foole [trusting] in his foolishnesse
Who so rewardeth euill for good, euil shall not depart from his house
The beginning of strife is, as when a man maketh an issue for water: therfore leaue of before the contention be medled with
The Lorde hateth as well hym that iustifieth the vngodly, as him that condempneth the innocent
Whereto hath a foole treasure in his hande to bye wisdome, seeing he hath no minde therto
He is a frende that alway loueth, and in aduersitie a man shall knowe who is his brother
Who so promiseth by the hande and is suretie for his neighbour, he is a foole
He that delighteth in sinne, loueth strife: and who so setteth his doore to hye, seeketh destruction
Who so hath a frowarde heart, obteyneth no good: and he that hath a double tongue, shall fall into mischiefe
He that begetteth a foole, begetteth his sorowe: and the father of a foole can haue no ioy
A mery heart make a lustie age: but a sorowfull minde dryeth vp the bones
The vngodly taketh gyftes out of the bosome, to wrest the wayes of iudgement
Wisdome [shineth] in the face of hym that hath vnderstanding: but the eyes of fooles wander throughout al landes
An vndiscrete sonne is a griefe vnto his father: and an heauinesse vnto his mother
Certaynely to condempne the iust is not good: nor to strike the gouernours whiche iudge rightly
A wyse man vseth fewe wordes, and a man of vnderstanding is of a pacient spirite
Yea, a very foole when he holdeth his tongue is counted wise: and he that stoppeth his lippes is esteemed prudent
18: Who so hath an earnest desire [to wysdome] he will sequester him selfe to seeke it, and occupie him selfe in all stedfastnesse & sounde doctrine
A foole hath no delight in vnderstanding: but onlye to vtter the fansies of his owne heart
When the vngodly commeth, then commeth also disdayne: and with the dishonest person commeth shame and dishonour
The wordes of a [wyse] mans mouth are lyke deepe waters: and the well of wisdome is like a full streame
It is not good to regarde the person of the vngodly, to ouerthrowe the righteous in iudgement
A fooles lippes come with brawling, and his mouth prouoketh vnto stripes
A fooles mouth is his owne destruction, and his lippes are the snare for his owne soule
The wordes of a slaunderer are very woundes, and go through vnto the innermost partes of the body
Who so is slouthfull in his labour, is the brother of hym that is a waster
The name of the Lorde is a strong castell, the righteous runneth vnto it and is in safegarde
The rich mans goodes are his strong citie, and as an high wall in his owne conceipt
Before destruction the heart of a man is proude: and before honour goeth humilitie
He that geueth sentence in a matter before he heare it, the same to hym is folly and shame
A good stomacke beareth out sickenesse: but the minde beyng sicke, who shall heale it
A wise heart possesseth knowledge, & a prudent eare seeketh vnderstanding
A mans gyft maketh an open way, to bryng hym before great men
The righteous declareth his owne cause first him selfe, and his neighbour commeth and tryeth hym
The lot causeth variaunce to ceasse: and parteth the mightie a sunder
Brethren beyng at variaunce are harder to be wonne then a strong citie, and their contentions are like the barre of a castell
A mans belly shalbe satisfied with the fruite of his owne mouth, and with the encrease of his lippes shall he be filled
Death and life are in the instrument of the tongue, and they that loue it, shall eate the fruite thereof
Who so findeth a wyfe, findeth a good thing, and receaueth fauour of the Lorde
The poore prayeth meekely: but the riche geueth a rough aunswere
A man that wyll haue frendes, must shewe hym selfe frendly: and there is a frende whiche is nearer then a brother
19: Better is the poore that liueth godly, then he that abuseth his lippes, and is a foole
The desire without discretion is not good: but [as] a man whiche hasteth with his feete offendeth
The foolishnesse of man paruerteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the Lorde
Riches maketh many frendes: but the poore is separated from his neighbour
A false witnesse shall not be vnpunished: and he that speaketh lyes shall not escape
The multitude hangeth vpon great men: and euery man fauoureth hym that geueth rewardes
All the brethren of the poore do hate hym, yea his owne frendes withdrawe them selues from hym: and he that geueth credence to wordes, getteth nothing
He that is wise loueth his owne soule, and kepeth vnderstanding, that he may prosper
A false witnesse shall not be vnpunished: and he that speaketh lyes shall perishe
Pleasure is not seemely for a foole: muche lesse for a bondman to haue rule of princes
A wyse man can put of displeasure, and it is his honour to let some faultes passe
The kynges displeasure is lyke the roaryng of a Lion: but his fauour is lyke the deawe vpon the grasse
An vndiscrete sonne is the heauinesse of his father, and a brawlyng wyfe is like the toppe of an house wherthrough it is euer dropping
House and riches may a man haue by the heritage of his elders: but a discrete woman is the gyft of the Lorde
Slouthfulnesse bryngeth sleepe, and a soule accustomed with craft, shall suffer hunger
Who so kepeth the commaundement, kepeth his owne soule: but he that regardeth not his wayes, shall dye
He that hath pitie vpon the poore, lendeth vnto the Lord: and looke what he layeth out, it shalbe payde hym agayne
Chasten thy sonne whyle there is hope: and let not thy soule spare for his crying
A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: and though thou [once] deliuer hym, thou must do it agayne
O geue eare vnto good counsayle, and be content to be refourmed, that thou mayest be wyse in the latter dayes
There are many deuises in a mans heart: neuerthelesse, the counsayle of the Lorde shall stande
It is a mans worship to do good: and a poore man is better then a lyer
The feare of the Lord [bringeth a man] to lyfe: and he shall rest the whole night in plenteousnesse without visitation of any plague
A slouthfull man shutteth his hande into his bosome, and wyll not take payne to put it to his mouth
If thou smytest a scornefull person, the ignoraunt shall take better heede: and if thou reprouest one that hath vnderstanding, he wyll be the wyser
He that hurteth his father, or shutteth out his mother, is a shamefull and an vnworthy sonne
My sonne heare no more the doctrine that leadeth thee vnto errours from the wordes of vnderstanding
A wicked witnesse mocketh iudgement: and the mouth of the vngodly deuoureth wickednesse
Iudgementes are ordeyned for the scornefull, and stripes for fooles backes
20: Wine maketh a man to be scornefull, & strong drinke causeth a man to be vnquiet: who so delighteth therin shall not be wyse
The feare of the king is as the roaring of a Lion, who so prouoketh hym vnto anger, offendeth against his owne soule
It is a mans honour to kepe him selfe from strife: but euery foole wyll be medling
A slouthfull body wyll not go to plow for colde of the winter: therefore shall he begge in sommer, and haue nothing
Counsayle in the heart of man is like deepe water: but a man of vnderstanding wyll drawe it out
Many there be that woulde be called good doers: but where shall one finde a faythfull man
The chyldren of the iust man which walketh vprightly, shalbe blessed after hym
A kyng that sitteth in the throne of iudgement, chaseth away all euyll with his looke
Who can say, I haue made my heart cleane, I am pure from [my] sinne
Two maner of wayghtes or two maner of measures, both these are abhomination vnto the Lorde
A chylde is knowen by his conuersation, whether his workes be pure and right
The eare to heare, the eye to see: the Lorde hath made them both
Loue not sleepe, lest thou come vnto pouertie: but open thyne eyes, that thou mayest haue bread inough
It is naught, it is naught (saith he that byeth): but when he commeth to his owne house, then he boasteth [of his peny worth.
There is golde, and a multitude of precious stones: but the lippes of knowledge are a precious iewell
Take his garment that is suretie for a straunger: and take a pledge of hym for the vnknowen sake
A man liketh the bread that is gotten with deceipt: but at the last his mouth shalbe filled with grauell
Thorowe counsayle, the thinges that men deuise are made strong: and with good aduise take warre in hande
The craftie deceiptfull bewrayeth secrete counsayle: therefore meddle not with hym that flattereth with his lips
Who so curseth his father and mother, his light shalbe put out in the depth of darknesse
The heritage that commeth hastylye at the first, shall not be blessed at the ende
Say not thou, I wyll recompence euyll: but put thy trust in the Lorde, and he shall deliuer thee
Diuers wayghtes are an abhomination vnto the Lord, and a false balaunce is not good
The Lord ordereth euery mans goinges: how can a man then vnderstand his owne way
It is a snare for a man to deuour that whiche is holy, and after the vowe to make inquirie
A wyse kyng disperseth the vngodly, and bringeth the wheele ouer them
The lanterne of the Lorde is the breath of man, searching all the inwarde partes of the body
Mercy and trueth preserueth the king, and with louing kindnes his seate is holden vp
The strength of young men is their worship, and a gray head is an honour vnto the aged
Blewe woundes driue away euyll, and stripes in the inwarde partes of the body
21: The kynges heart is in the hand of the Lord, lyke as are the riuers of water, he maye turne it whyther soeuer he wyll
Euery mans way seemeth right in his owne eyes: but the Lorde pondereth the heart
To do righteousnes and iudgement, is more acceptable to the Lorde then sacrifice
An high looke, a proude heart, and the plowing of the vngodly is sinne
The deuises of one that is diligent, bring plenteousnesse: but he that is vnaduised, commeth vnto pouertie
To hoorde vp riches with a deceiptfull tongue, is vanitie tossed to and fro of them that seeke death
The robberies of the vngodly shalbe their owne destruction: for they wyll not do the thing that is right
The way of the vngodly is frowarde and straunge: but of the pure man his worke is right
It is better to dwel in a corner on the house toppe, then with a brawling woman in a wide house
The soule of the vngodly wisheth euyll, and his neighbour findeth no fauour in his eyes
When the scornefull is punished, the ignoraunt take the better heede: and when the wyse is instructed, he wyll receaue vnderstanding
The righteous man wysely considereth the house of the wicked, and for their wickednesse [God] ouerthroweth the vngodly
Who so stoppeth his eares at the crying of the poore, he shall crye hym selfe and not be hearde
A priuie rewarde pacifieth displeasure: and a gyft in the bosome [stylleth] furiousnesse
The iust delighteth in doing the thing that is right: but destruction shalbe to the workers of wickednesse
The man that wandereth out of the way of wysdome, shall remaine in the congregation of the dead
He that hath pleasure in bankettes shalbe a poore man: and whoso delighteth in wyne and delicates, shall not be riche
The vngodly shalbe a raunsome for the righteous: and the wicked for the iust
It is better to dwell in the wyldernesse, then with a chydyng and an angrye woman
In a wise mans house there is a great treasure and oyle: but a foolishe body spendeth vp all
Who so foloweth righteousnesse and mercy, findeth both life, righteousnesse, and honour
A wyse man skaleth the citie of the mightie, & ouerthroweth the strength wherein they trusted
Who so kepeth his mouth and his tongue, the same kepeth his soule from troubles
He that is proude and arrogant; is called a scorner, whiche in his wrath worketh presumptuously
The desire of the slouthfull kylleth him: for his handes wyll not labour
He coueteth greedyly all day long: but the righteous geueth and spareth not
The sacrifice of the vngodly is abhomination: howe muche more when they offer the thing that is gotten with wickednesse
A false witnesse shall perishe: but [a good] man speaketh constantly what he hath hearde
An vngodly man hardeneth his face: but the iust refourmeth his owne way
There is no wysdome, there is no vnderstanding, there is no counsayle against the Lorde
The horse is prepared against the day of battayle: but the Lorde geueth victorie
22: A good name is more to be desired then great riches: and louing fauour [is better] then siluer and golde
The riche and poore meete together: the Lorde is the maker of them all
A wyse man seeth the plague, and hydeth hym selfe: but the foolishe go on still, and are punished
By humilitie and the feare of the Lorde, [commeth] riches, honour, and life
Thornes and snares are in the way of the frowarde: but he that doth kepe his soule, wyll flee farre from them
Teache a chylde what way he should go: for he shall not leaue it when he is olde
The ryche ruleth the poore, and the borower is seruaunt to the lender
He that soweth wickednes, shal reape wickednes: and the rodde of his anger shall fayle
He that hath a bountifull eye, shalbe blessed: for he geueth of his bread to the poore
Cast out the scorneful man, and so shal strife go out with hym: yea variaunce and sclaunder shall ceasse
Who so loueth cleannes of heart, for the grace of his lippes the kyng shalbe his frende
The eyes of the Lord preserue knowledge: and he ouerthroweth the wordes of the transgressours
The slouthfull body saith there is a Lion without: I might be slaine in the streate
The mouth of straunge women is a deepe pit: wherein he falleth that the Lorde is angrye withall
Foolishnes is bounde in the heart of the chylde: and the rodde of correction shall driue it away
Who so doth a poore man wrong, to increase his owne [riches] and geueth vnto the ryche, at the last commeth to pouertie hym selfe
Bowe downe thyne eare, and heare the wordes of the wise: applie thy mind vnto my doctrine
For it is a pleasaunt thing if thou kepe them in thyne heart, and order them in thy lippes
That thou mayest put thy trust in the Lorde, I haue shewed thee this day the thing that thou knowest
Haue not I warned thee very oft with counsayle and learning
That I might make thee knowe the trueth, that thou with the veritie mightest aunswere them that sende vnto thee
Rob not the poore, because he is poore: and oppresse not the simple in iudgement
For the Lorde him selfe wyll defende their cause, and do violence vnto them that haue vsed violence
Make no frendship with an angrye wylfull man, and walke not with the furious
Lest thou learne his wayes, and receaue hurt to thy soule
Be not thou one of them that binde their hande vpon promise, and are suretie for waightie causes
For if thou hast nothing to pay, they shall take away thy bed from vnder thee
Thou shalt not remoue the auncient lande marke, whiche thy fore elders haue set
Seest thou not that they which be diligent in their businesse stande before kinges, & not among the simple people
23: When thou sittest to eate with a noble man, consider diligently what is set before thee
Measure thyne appetite if it be gredyly set
Be not desirous of his daintie meates, for meate begyleth and deceaueth
Take not ouer great trauayle to be riche, beware of suche a purpose
Wylt thou set thyne eye vpon the thing which sodenly vanisheth away? For riches make them selues wynges, and take their flight lyke an Egle into the ayre
Eate thou not the bread of hym that hath an euyll eye: neither desire thou his daintie meate
For as though he thought it in his heart, he saith, eate and drinke: where as his heart is not with thee
The morsels that thou hast eaten shalt thou parbreake, and loose those sweete wordes
Tell nothing into the eares of a foole: for he wyll despise the wysdome of thy wordes
Remoue not the olde lande marke, and come not within the fielde of the fatherlesse
For their redeemer is mightie, euen he shall defend their cause against thee
Applye thyne heart vnto correction, and thyne eare to the wordes of knowledge
Withholde not correction from the chylde: for if thou beatest hym with the rodde, he shall not dye thereof
If thou smyte hym with the rodde, thou shalt deliuer his soule from hell
My sonne if thy heart receaue wysdome, my heart also shall reioyce
Yea my raynes shalbe very glad, if thy lippes speake the thing that is right
Let not thyne heart be ielous to folowe sinners, but kepe thee styll in the feare of the Lorde all the day long
For veryly there is an ende, and thy pacient abiding shall not be cut of
My sonne geue eare and be wyse, and set straight thyne heart in the way [of the Lorde.
Kepe not company with wine bibbers, and riotous eaters of fleshe
For suche as be drunkardes and riotours shall come to pouertie: and he that is geuen to muche sleepe, shall go with a ragged coate
Geue eare vnto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is olde
Purchase trueth, wysdome, nurture, and vnderstanding, and sell them not
The father of the righteous shall greatly reioyce: and he that begetteth a wyse chylde, shall haue ioy of hym
[Do so that] thy father and mother may be glad of thee, and that she that bare thee may reioyce
My sonne geue me thyne heart, and let thyne eyes haue pleasure in my wayes
For an whore is a deepe graue, and a straunge woman is a narowe pit
She lyeth in wayte as for a pray, and increaseth the transgressours amongst men
Who hath wo? who hath sorowe? who hath strife? who hath brawling? and who hath woundes without a cause
Or who hath red eyes? euen they that be euer at the wine, & seeke excesse
Looke not thou vpon the wine howe red it is, and what a colour it geueth in the glasse
It goeth downe sweetely, but at the last it byteth like a serpent, and stingeth lyke an adder
Thyne eyes shall beholde straunge women, and thyne heart shall vtter lewde thinges
Yea thou shalt be as though thou layest in the middest of the sea, or slepest vppon the top of the maste of a ship
They haue beaten me [shalt thou say] and I was not sicke, they haue stricken me, and I felt it not: When I am well wakened, I wil go to the drinke again
24: Be not thou enuious to folow wicked men, and desire not to be among them
For their heart imagineth to do hurt, and their lippes talke mischiefe
Thorowe wysdome is an house buylded, & with vnderstanding is it set vp
Thorowe discretion shall the chaumbers be filled with all costly and pleasaunt riches
A wise man is [euer] strong: yea a man of vnderstanding increaseth strength
For with discretion must warres be taken in hand: and where as are many that can geue counsaile, there is health
Wysdome is to hye a thyng for a foole: for he dare not open his mouth in the gate
He that imagineth mischiefe, maye well be called an vngratious person
The wicked thought of the foolishe is sinne: and the scornefull is an abhomination vnto men
If thou be faynt in the day of aduersitie, thy strength is small
Deliuer them that are drawen vnto death, and ceasse not to preserue them that are led to be slayne

If thou wylt say, beholde I knewe not of it: doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? And he that kepeth thy soule, knoweth he it not? Shall not he also recompence euery man according to his workes
My sonne, eate thou hony because it is good, and the hony combe, for it is sweete vnto thy mouth
So [sweete] shal the knowledge of wysdome be vnto thy soule when thou hast found it: and there shalbe hope, and thy hope shall not be cut of
Laye no priuie wayte (O wicked man) against the house of the righteous, and spoyle not his resting place
For a iust man falleth seuen tymes, and ryseth vp agayne: but the vngodly fall into mischiefe
Reioyce not thou at the fall of thyne enemie, and let not thyne heart be glad when he stumbleth
Lest the Lorde when he seeth it be angry, and turne his wrath from hym [vnto thee.
Fret not thy selfe because of the malitious, neither be enuious at the wicked
For the wicked shall haue no posteritie, and the candle of the vngodly shalbe put out
My sonne, feare thou the Lorde and the kyng, and kepe no company with them that slide backe [from his feare:
For their destruction shall rise sodainlye: and who knoweth the aduersitie that may come from them both
It is not good to haue respect of any person in iudgement
He that saith to the vngodly thou art righteous, hym shall the people curse, yea the comminaltie shall abhorre him
But they that rebuke [the vngodly] in them doth God delight, and a rych blessing shall come vpon them
Euery man shall kisse his lippes that geueth a good aunswere
Make redie thy worke that is without, and looke well vnto that whiche thou hast in the fielde: and then buylde thyne house
Be not a false witnesse against thy neighbour, and speake no falsehood with thy lippes
Say not, I wyll handle hym euen as he hath dealt with me: and wyll rewarde euery man according to his deedes
I went by the fielde of the slouthfull, and by the vineyarde of the foolishe man
And lo, it was all couered with nettles, and stoode full of thornes, and the stone wall was broken downe
This I sawe, and considered it well: I looked vpon it, and toke it for a warning
Yea sleepe on styll [I say] a litle, slumber a litle, folde thy handes together yet a litle
So shall pouertie come vnto thee as one that trauayleth by the way, and necessitie lyke a weaponed man
25: These are also parables of Solomon, which the men of Ezekia king of Iuda copied out
It is the glory of God to kepe a thing secrete: but the kynges honour is to searche out a thing
The heauen is hye, the earth is deepe: and the kinges heart is vnsearcheable
Take the drosse from the siluer, and there shalbe a vessell for the siner
Take away the vngodly from the kyng: and his seate shalbe stablished with righteousnesse
Put not foorth thy selfe in the presence of the king, and preasse not into the place of great men
For better is it, that it be sayde vnto thee, come vp hyther: then thou to be put lower in the presence of the priuce whom thou seest with thyne eyes
Be not hastie to go to lawe: lest haplye thou knowest not what to do when thy neighbour hath confounded thee
Handle thy matter with thy neighbour himselfe, and discouer not thy secrete to another
Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thy infamie do not ceasse
A worde spoken in due season, is lyke apples of golde in a graued worke of siluer
Who so reproueth a wyse man that hath an obedient eare, is as a golden earring, and an ornament of fine golde
As the colde of snowe in the tyme of haruest: so is a faythfull messenger to them that sende hym, for he refresheth his maisters mynde
Whoso maketh great boastes and geueth nothing, is lyke cloudes and winde without rayne
With pacience is a prince pacified, and with a softe tongue is rigorousnesse broken
If thou findest honie, eate so muche as is sufficient for thee: lest thou be ouer full, and parbreake it out agayne
Withdrawe thy foote from thy neighbours house: lest he be werie of thee, and so hate thee
Whoso beareth false witnesse against his neighbour, he is a very club, a sworde, and a sharpe arrowe
The confidence that is put in an vnfaythfull man in tyme of trouble, is like a broken tooth, and a sliding foote
Who so taketh away a mans garment in the colde weather, is like vineger vpon lime, or lyke hym that singeth songues to an heauie heart
If thyne enemie hunger, feede hym, if he thirst, geue him drinke
For so shalt thou heape coles of fire vpon his head, and the Lorde shall rewarde thee
The northwinde dryueth away the rayne: euen so doth an angry countenaunce a backbiters tongue
It is better to sit in a corner vpon the house toppe, then with a brawling woman in a wide house
Good newes from a straunge countrey, are as colde water to a thirstie soule
A righteous man fallyng downe before the vngodly, is like a troubled wel, and a spring that is corrupted
As it is not good to eate to muche honye, so curiously to searche the glory of heauenly thinges, is not commendable
He that can not rule him selfe, is like a citie whiche is broken downe and hath no walles
26: Lyke as snowe is [not meete] in sommer and rayne in haruest: euen so is worship vnseemely for a foole
As the byrde and the swalowe take their flight and flee here and there: so the curse that is geuen in vayne, shall not light vpon a man
Unto the horse belongeth a whip, to the asse a brydle: and a rod to the fooles backe
Geue not the foole an aunswere after his foolishnes, lest thou become like vnto him
But make the foole an aunswere to his foolishnesse, lest he be wyse in his owne conceipt
[As he that] cutteth of [his messengers] feete endamageth himselfe: so doth he that committeth a message to a foole
Like as in a lame man his legges are not equall: euen so is a parable in a fooles mouth
He that setteth a foole in hye dignitie, that is euen as if a man would bynde a stone in a sling
As is a thorne in the hande of a drunkarde: so is a parable in a fooles mouth
The mightie that fourmed al thinges, rewardeth the fooles & transgressours
Like as the dogge turneth agayne to his owne vomite: euen so a foole beginneth his foolishnes agayne afreshe
If thou seest a man that is wise in his owne conceipt: there is more hope in a foole, then in hym
The slouthfull saith, there is a lion in the way, and a lion in the middest of the streates
Like as the doore turneth about vpon the hynges: euen so doth the slouthfull walter him selfe in his bed
The slouthfull body thrusteth his hande into his bosome, and it greeueth hym to put it agayne to his mouth
The sluggarde thinketh him selfe wiser then seuen men that sit and teache
Who so goeth by and medleth with other mens strife: he is like one that taketh a dogge by the eares
As he that fayneth him selfe mad, casteth firebrandes, deadly arrowes and dartes
So doth a dissembler with his neighbour, and saith, am not I in sport
Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: euen so where the talebearer is taken away, there the strife ceasseth
As coles kindle heate, and wood the fire: euen so doth a brawling felowe stirre vp variaunce
A talebearers wordes are lyke men that strike with hammers, and they pearse the inwarde partes of the body
Burning lippes and a wicked heart, are like a potsharde couered with siluer drosse
An enemie wyll dissemble with his lippes, and layeth vp deceipt in his heart
But when he speaketh fayre, beleue hym not: for there are seuen abhominations in his heart
Hatred maye be couered by deceipt: but the malice therof shalbe shewed before the whole congregation
Who so diggeth vp a pit, shal fall therin: and he that rolleth vp a stone, it wyl returne vpon hym
A lying tongue hateth the afflicted: and a flattering mouth worketh mischiefe
27: Make not thy boast of to morowe: for thou knowest not what a day may bring foorth
Let another man prayse thee, and not thyne owne mouth, yea other folkes, and not thyne owne lippes
The stone is heauie, and the sande wayghtie: but a fooles wrath is heauier then them both
Wrath is a cruell thing, and furiousnesse is a very tempest: but who is able to abide enuie
Open rebuke, is better then secrete loue
Faythfull are the woundes of a louer: but the kysses of an enemie are cruell
He that is full, abhorreth an honye combe: but vnto hym that is hungrye, euery sowre thing is sweete
He that oft times flitteth, is like a byrd that forsaketh her nest
Baulme and sweete incense make the heart merie: so sweete is that frende that geueth counsell from the heart
Thyne owne frende and thy fathers frende see thou forsake not, and go not into thy brothers house in tyme of thy trouble: for better is a frende at hand, then a brother farre of
My sonne be wyse, and make me a glad heart, that I may make aunswere vnto my rebukers
A wyse man seing the plague, wyll hide hym selfe: as for fooles they go on styll and suffer harme
Take his garment that is suretie for a straunger, and take a pledge of hym for the vnknowen sake
He that is to hastie to praise his neighbour aboue measure, shalbe taken as one that geueth hym an euyll report
A brawling woman and the roofe of the house dropping in a raynie day, may well be compared together
He that stilleth her, stilleth the winde, and stoppeth the smell of the oyntment in his hande
Like as one iron whetteth another, so doth one man comfort another
Whoso kepeth his figge tree, shall eate the fruites thereof: so he that wayteth vpon his maister, shall come to honour
Like as in one water there appeare diuers faces: euen so diuers men haue diuers heartes
Hell and destruction are neuer full: euen so the eyes of men can neuer be satisfied
As is the fining pot for the siluer, and the furnace for golde: so is a man tryed by the mouth of him that prayseth him
Though thou shouldest bray a foole with a pestel in a morter like furmentie corne: yet wyll not his foolishnes go from hym
Be thou diligent to knowe the state of thy cattell thy selfe, and loke well to thy flockes
For riches abideth not alway, and the crowne endureth not for euer
The hay groweth, the grasse commeth vp, and hearbes are gathered in the mountaynes
The lambes shall clothe thee, and for the goates thou shalt haue money to thy husbandry
Thou shalt haue goates milke inough to feede thee, to vpholde thy housholde, and to sustayne thy maydens
28: The vngodly fleeth when no man pursueth him: but the righteous are bolde as a Lion
For the wickednes of the lande, the prince is oft chaunged: but thorowe a man of vnderstanding and wysdome, a realme endureth long
One poore man oppressing another by violence, is like a raging rayne that destroyeth the fruite
They that forsake the lawe, prayse the vngodly: but such as kepe the lawe are greeued at them
Wicked men vnderstande not iudgement: but they that seeke the Lord, vnderstande all thinges
Better is he that walketh in his vprightnes: then he that peruerteth his wayes, and is riche
Who so kepeth the lawe, is a chylde of vnderstanding: but he that is a companion of riotous men, shameth his father
He that by vsurie and vniust gaynes gathereth riches: he shall lay them in store for a man that will pitie the poore
He that turneth away his eare from hearing the lawe, his prayer shalbe abhominable
Who so causeth the righteous to go astray by an euill way, shall fall into his owne pit: but the iust shall haue the good in possession
The riche man thinketh hym selfe to be wise: but the poore that hath vnderstandyng can perceaue hym well inough
When righteous men do reioyce, there is great glory: but when the wicked come vp, the man is tryed
He that hydeth his sinnes, shall not prosper: but whoso knowledgeth them and forsaketh them, shall haue mercy
Well is hym that standeth alway in awe: as for hym that hardeneth his heart, he shall fall into mischiefe
As a roaring Lion and an hungrye Beare, so is an vngodly prince ouer the poore people
Where the prince is without vnderstanding, there is great oppression and wrong: but if he hateth couetousnes, he shall long raigne
He that by violence shedeth any mans blood, shalbe a runnagate vnto his graue, and no man shalbe able to succour hym
Whoso leadeth an innocent life, shalbe saued: but he that goeth frowarde wayes, shall once haue a fall
He that tylleth his lande shall haue plenteousnes of bread: but he that foloweth idle persons, shall haue pouertie inough
A faythfull man shalbe fylled with blessinges, and he that maketh haste to be riche, shall not be vngyltie
To haue respect of persons [in iudgement] is not good, for that man wyll do wrong, yea euen for a peece of bread
He that wyll be riche all to soone, hath an euyll eye: and considereth not that pouertie shall come vpon hym
He that folowyng my preceptes rebuketh a man, shall fynde more fauour at the last then he that flattereth hym
Who so robbeth his father and mother, and sayth it is no sinne: the same is the companion of a destroyer
He that is of a proude stomacke stirreth vp strife: but he that putteth his trust in the Lorde shalbe well fed
He that trusteth in his owne heart is a foole: but he that dealeth wisely shalbe safe
He that geueth vnto the poore shall not lacke: but he that hydeth his eyes from them, shall haue many a curse
When the vngodly are come vp, men are fayne to hide themselues: but when they perishe, the ryghteous encrease
29: He that is stifnecked and wyll not be refourmed, shall sodaynly be destroyed without any helpe
When the ryghteous are in aucthoritie the people do reioyce: but when the wicked beare rule, the people mourne
Who so loueth wisdome, maketh his father a glad man: but he that kepeth companie with harlottes, spendeth away that he hath
With [true] iudgement the kyng stablissheth the lande: but yf he be a man that oppresse the people with gatherynges, he turneth it vpside downe
Who so flattereth his neighbour, layeth a net for his feete
The sinne of the wicked is his owne snare: but the ryghteous doth syng and reioyce
The righteous considereth the cause of the poore: but the vngodly regardeth no vnderstandyng
Scornefull men bryng a citie into a snare: but wise men turne away wrath
If a wise man contendeth with a foole: whether he be angry or laugh, there is no rest
The bloodthirstie hate the righteous: but the iust seeke his soule
A foole vttereth all his mynde at once: but a wyse man kepeth it in tyll afterwarde
If a prince delight in lyes, all his seruauntes are vngodly
The poore and the lender meete together, and the Lorde lyghteneth both their eyes
The seate of the kyng that faithfully iudgeth the poore, shall continue sure for euermore
The rodde and correction geueth wisdome: but a childe left to his owne will, bryngeth his mother to shame
When the vngodly are multiplied, wickednesse encreaseth: but the ryghteous shall see their fall
Nurture thy sonne with correction, and thou shalt be at rest: yea, he shall do thee good at thine heart
When the worde of God is not preached, the people perishe: but well is hym that kepeth the lawe
A [stubbourne] seruaunt wyll not be the better for wordes: for though he vnderstande, yet will he not regarde them
Seest thou a man that is hastie to speake vnaduisedly? there is more hope in a foole then in hym
He that delicately bryngeth vp his seruaunt from a chylde, shall make hym his maister at length
An angry man stirreth vp strife, and he that beareth euyll will in his mynde doth much euyll
After pryde commeth a fall: but a lowly spirite bryngeth great worshyp
Who so is partner with a thiefe, hateth his owne soule: he heareth blasphemie and telleth it not foorth
He that feareth men shall haue a fall: but who so putteth his trust in the Lorde, is without daunger
Many there be that seke the princes fauour: but euery mans iudgement commeth from the Lorde
The righteous abhorreth the vngodlye: and the wicked hateth hym that is in the ryght way
30: And the prophecie that the same man spake vnto Ithiel, euen vnto Ithiel and Uchal
Surely I am more foolishe then any man, and haue no mans vnderstandyng
I neuer learned wisdome, nor had knowledge of holy thynges

Who hath clymed vp into heauen, and come downe from thence? who hath holden the wynde fast in his hande? who hath gathered together the waters in a garment? who hath established all the endes of the worlde: what is his name, and what is his sonnes name, yf thou canst tell
Euery worde of God is pure: he is a shielde vnto all them that put their trust in hym
Put thou nothyng vnto his wordes, lest he reproue thee, and thou be founde a lyar
Two thinges haue I required of thee, denie me them not before I dye
Remoue farre fro me vanitie and lyes, geue me neither pouertie nor riches, only graunt me a necessary lyuyng
Lest peraduenture I beyng full, shoulde denie thee, and say, who is the Lorde? or beyng oppressed with pouertie fall to stealyng, and forswere the name of my God
Accuse not a seruaunt vnto his maister, lest he speake euyll of thee, and thou be hurt
There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not blesse their mother
There is a generation that thynke them selues cleane, and yet is not cleansed from their filthinesse
There is a generation that hath a proude loke, and doth cast vp their eye lyddes
